title: Check Around and find out
reviewNotes: Saved montage and captions reviewed with native complete board checks. Begin after Kc8 at 86 seconds in the complete nine-piece later diagram. Rc1+/Kb8/Ka6 is proved against all twelve White promotions, each met by actual Ba7 mate; the white bishop and all four seventh-rank pawns are preserved. d8=Q is illustrated by the source; f8=N and h8=Q are explicitly independent comparison defenses. This finite legal mate proof does not certify the earlier long bishop-and-rook shepherd, premature promotion interpositions or claims of a forced route from the original board.
transcript: White is mocking us. He brought all of these pawns just one step away from getting a queen without actually getting one just to make fun of black. But what white failed to realize is that it just [music] dug his own grave because in this position black has one of the most amazing resources I've ever seen. The first move is pretty obvious. It's the only check we have available, bishop to F4. This attacks the king and forces it to either move here or to get checkmated in just one move. So naturally the king goes to C8. But now black can follow up with rook to C1 check. And actually the bishop and rook are collaborating in pushing the king to D8. As long as black keeps giving checks, white is not going to be on time to promote any of the pawns to a new queen. So black gives another check. And now again the king is forced to move to the E8 square. And black can repeat this process two more times to make sure that the king reaches the corner of the board. And now from here it might seem like there's no way to make progress because now if you try to bring the bishop back and give a checkmate like [music] this, white is simply going to promote to a new queen and then sacrifice that same queen to avoid the checkmate and make sure that it can save a draw. But black is not done kicking this king around and he plays bishop to G7 check, now forcing the king to step in front of the line of the rook allowing a discovered check like this. And yes, you guessed it. Black now starts to shepherd the king to the other side of the board with the same exact pattern. And eventually we reach a position where the king is on B8. And again it might seem like white is simply out of the woods. If you give another check with the bishop, we're going to repeat the same pattern. But black has the brilliant king to A6 patiently allowing white to get a new [music] queen. But after white does that, bishop to A7 is going to be an incredible checkmate. If you love incredible [music] chess, follow for more.
